content: 1. Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Fumarate: Follow the manufacturer’s color-coding for the sequence of administration. This combination is not recommended for premenarchal individuals. 2. Ethinyl Estradiol and Fezolinetant: Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels and effects of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it raises fezolinetant’s AUC and peak plasma concentration when co-administered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 3. Ethinyl Estradiol and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir/Dasabuvir (DSC): Co-administration is contraindicated due to an unspecified interaction mechanism that increases toxicity. Clinical trials have shown significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, some >20x ULN) when ethinyl estradiol is combined with these drugs. Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before initiating hepatitis C combination therapy and restart approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 4. Tranexamic Acid and Ethinyl Estradiol: Co-administration is contraindicated due to pharmacodynamic synergism, which increases the risk of thrombosis. Avoid combining tranexamic acid with combination hormonal contraceptives. 5. Acitretin and Norethindrone Acetate: Acitretin decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Amobarbital and Ethinyl Estradiol: Amobarbital reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, so nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 7. Ethinyl Estradiol and Anastrozole: Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use of anastrozole with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 8. Apalutamide and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Apalutamide decreases the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or substitute alternative drugs. Hormonal contraceptives may lose efficacy, so nonhormonal contraception is advised. 9. Armodafinil and Ethinyl Estradiol: Armodafinil reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 10. Ferrous Fumarate and Baloxavir Marboxil: Ferrous fumarate decreases baloxavir absorption by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Separate administration by at least four hours if co-administration is necessary. 11. Atazanavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 12. Belzutifan and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Belzutifan decreases the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to contraceptive failure or breakthrough bleeding. Nonhormonal contraception is advised. 13. Bosentan and Ethinyl Estradiol: Bosentan reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 14. Carbamazepine and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: Carbamazepine reduces the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable in this context, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 15. Brigatinib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Brigatinib induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing ethinyl estradiol levels and efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 16. Butabarbital and Ethinyl Estradiol: Butabarbital reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 17. Calaspargase Pegol and Ethinyl Estradiol: Co-administration is not recommended due to potential indirect interactions. Use non-oral contraceptive methods for females of childbearing potential. 18. Dexamethasone and Ethinyl Estradiol: Dexamethasone reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 19. Efavirenz and Ethinyl Estradiol: Efavirenz reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 20. Ethinyl Estradiol and Elagolix: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of elagolix through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended during treatment and for one week after discontinuation. 21. Ferrous Fumarate and Doxycycline/Minocycline/Oxytetracycline: Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of these antibiotics in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Fosamprenavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Co-administration may alter hormone levels and reduce virologic response. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 23. Phenobarbital/Phenytoin/Primidone and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 24. Quinidine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Quinidine increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Rifabutin/Rifampin and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 26. Ethinyl Estradiol and Ranolazine: Ethinyl estradiol increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Repotrectinib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Repotrectinib induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing ethinyl estradiol levels and efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 28. Ivosidenib and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Ivosidenib reduces the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 29. Lenolisib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Letrozole and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of letrozole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid concurrent use. 31. Mifepristone and Ethinyl Estradiol: Mifepristone increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Mitotane and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: Mitotane reduces the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 33. Omacetaxine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Omacetaxine reduces the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 34. Oxcarbazepine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Oxcarbazepine reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 35. Ranolazine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ethinyl estradiol increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Repotrectinib and Ethinyl Estradiol: Repotrectinib induces CYP3A4 metabolism, reducing ethinyl estradiol levels and efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 37. Rifabutin/Rifampin and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 38. Ferrous Fumarate and Levofloxacin/Moxifloxacin/Gemifloxacin: Ferrous fumarate reduces the absorption of these antibiotics in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Griseofulvin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Griseofulvin reduces the levels and effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 40. Ethinyl Estradiol and Heparin/Enoxaparin: Ethinyl estradiol reduces the efficacy of these anticoagulants, increasing the risk of thromboembolic disorders. Co-administration is contraindicated. 41. Idelalisib and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Idelalisib increases the levels and effects of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lopinavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Lopinavir alters estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 43. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 44. Mavacamten and Ethinyl Estradiol/Norethindrone Acetate: Mavacamten reduces the levels and effects of these drugs by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 45. Ethinyl Estradiol and Metyrapone: Ethinyl estradiol reduces metyrapone efficacy. Discontinue estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration. 46. Nelfinavir and Ethinyl Estradiol: Nelfinavir alters estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 47. Omacetaxine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Omacetaxine reduces the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 48. Phenobarbital/Phenytoin/Primidone and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 49. Quinidine and Ethinyl Estradiol: Quinidine increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Rifabutin/Rifampin and Norethindrone Acetate/Ethinyl Estradiol: These drugs reduce the levels and effects of hormonal contraceptives by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraception is recommended.
